question: When did the Indigo Revolt of Bengal take place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1859 C.E.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indigo Revolt** of Bengal took place in **1859 C.E.**
 
• It was a peasant movement and subsequent uprising of indigo farmers against the oppressive policies of the British planters.
 
• The revolt was sparked by the exploitative practices of the British planters who forced farmers to grow indigo under harsh conditions and offered extremely low prices for their produce.
 
• The rebellion was marked by non-violent protests, social boycotts, and refusal to sow indigo.
 
• The movement gained significant attention and led to the formation of the Indigo Commission in 1860, which ultimately resulted in the decline of indigo plantations in Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indigo Commission** was set up by the British government in response to the revolt, and it recommended the cessation of the oppressive indigo farming practices.
 
• The Indigo Revolt is considered one of the early forms of organized peasant resistance against British colonial rule in India.
 
• Key figures in the revolt included **Biswanath Sardar** and **Digambar Biswas**, who played crucial roles in mobilizing the farmers.
 
• The revolt inspired subsequent agrarian movements in India and highlighted the need for agrarian reforms.
